proposed_widenings.name: passive_initiative_trigger family for ClassFeatureMechanics
proposed_widenings.justification: The feature fires automatically when the bard rolls Initiative — not on player activation. The existing ClassFeatureMechanics only has the 'activation' family, which models player-initiated use of a feature with an explicit cost. There is no family for 'passive: fires automatically when a named game event occurs'. This requires a new mechanics family (e.g. 'passive_trigger' or 'initiative_trigger') with a trigger field pointing to the game event (initiative_window) instead of an activationCost.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.

proposed_widenings.name: refill_resource_to_floor (new ClassFeatureEffect variant)
proposed_widenings.justification: The effect is not grant_extra_action or heal_hp — it sets the bard's Bardic Inspiration use count to at least N (floor=2) if currently below that floor. This is a conditional partial-refill of a named external resource, not a self-heal or extra action. No existing ClassFeatureEffect variant covers 'conditionally top up a separate resource to a minimum value'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that

notes: The unit is fully deterministic and in-scope for core mechanics (no DM agenda). Both gaps are structural: (1) the class feature family model requires a passive/auto-triggered variant keyed to an initiative_window rather than player activation, and (2) the effect vocabulary needs a 'refill named resource to floor N' shape. The Bardic Inspiration resource itself (modeled separately as bard_bardic_inspiration_l1) would be the target of the refill. No honest encoding is possible within the current surface.
